Name: coverage_currency_coupling
Title: Concentration Is the Common Currency: Self-Editing Memory and Prompt Optimization Both Buy pass@1 by Spending Solve-Set Coverage, and Stacking Them Pays Twice
Short Hypothesis: Both halves of the memory+prompt-optimizer stack act on the *same* axis: they are distribution-concentration devices, not information-addition devices. Concretely: (i) retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions each raise pass@1 while shrinking the set of tasks solvable with any of k samples, so each advantage decays or reverses by moderate k; (ii) the concentration is a mode *shift*, not mere sharpening — matching decoding diversity by temperature does not restore coverage; (iii) they concentrate onto *different* modes, which is why they look complementary at k=1, but composing them in one prompt (naively or co-adapted) compounds the coverage loss while the pass@1 gains sub-add — coupling pays twice and gets less than double. The constructive corollary, and the reason the track's "division of labour" intuition is right but misplaced: the labour must be divided *across the rollout portfolio*, not across prompt slots. A heterogeneous portfolio (some rollouts plain, some memory-conditioned, some optimizer-conditioned) beats any homogeneous conditioning at matched total budget.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **Prompt optimization.** MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695) and GEPA (arXiv 2507.19457) treat a prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over it with Bayesian or reflective-evolutionary updates, reporting single-sample validation accuracy at every step. Neither the search objective nor the reported result is sampling-aware: a candidate that concentrates mass onto an already-reachable solution is indistinguishable, under their metric, from one that makes a new solution reachable. Our claim is that this distinction is exactly what the optimizer is silently trading away, and it is the reason the prior track finding "the optimizer's gain was redistribution, not accuracy" recurs.

(2) **Agentic experience memory.** ExpeL, Reflexion, A-Mem (2502.12110), AgentFly/Memento (2508.16153), MemGen (2509.24704), ReasoningBank and the 2026 wave all report pass@1 with a bank versus without, at fixed decoding budget. None reports a pass@k or solve-set coverage curve, so none separates "memory supplied a solution otherwise unreachable" from "memory made a reachable solution more likely."

(3) **Concurrent work on memory and multi-sample inference — the live collision.** "When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?" (arXiv 2605.28224) argues that injected positive prior facts bias tool-use agents toward consistency, producing a diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff no retrieval policy escapes. This is the closest existing statement of our memory-side phenomenon and we treat it as prior work, not as a gap. It is qualitative about the tradeoff (diversity and efficiency), it does not measure whether the *set of solvable instances* shrinks, it does not distinguish sharpening from mode shift (no diversity-matched decoding control), it contains no prompt optimizer, and its "any positive prior triggers it" account makes a prediction we can falsify with a length-matched decoy arm. "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (arXiv 2505.16067, ACL 2026) documents *experience-following*: high input-memory similarity yields highly similar outputs, with error propagation over time — a mechanism-level precedent for homogenization, framed as long-horizon degradation rather than coverage accounting.

(4) **Diversity collapse from training.** Outcome-based Exploration for LLM Reasoning (2509.06941) and Post-training LLMs for Diverse High-Quality Outputs (2509.04784) establish pass@1-up / pass@k-down for gradient updates; R-Diverse (2602.13103) and DyJR (2603.16157) attack the same collapse inside self-play and RLVR training loops; "Exploratory Memory-Augmented LLM Agent" (2602.23008) asserts that static memory cannot capture the diversity needed for continued improvement and fixes it with joint RL. All of these are weight-space interventions or propose fixes; none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue, and none asks whether *prompt optimization* — the other half of the stack — carries the same signature.

(5) **Retrieval × aggregation.** Inference Scaling for Bridging Retrieval and Augmented Generation (2412.10684) notes retrieval quality interacting negatively with self-consistency in single-turn RAG QA and proposes passage permutation; "Self-Consistency Is Losing Its Edge" (2511.00751) attributes diminishing sampling returns to model capability, a competing explanation we control for by measuring the unconditioned curve on the same models; ICL-diversity work (2404.16807) shows in-context examples reduce *lexical* diversity in single-turn generation.

Our contribution is not "memory reduces diversity" — 2605.28224 is concurrent on that. It is the coverage accounting (what is actually lost, and whether it is lost or merely made rarer), the sharpening-vs-shifting adjudication, and the claim that concentration is the *common currency* of both halves of the memory+optimizer stack, which turns the track's division-of-labour question upside down: complementarity is real, but only harvestable across rollouts.
Abstract: Agent frameworks now bolt a self-editing memory onto a prompt optimizer and report a higher single-sample success rate. That number cannot tell you whether either component supplied a solution the agent could not otherwise find, or merely made one it could already find more probable. We hypothesize that both components are concentration devices operating on the same axis, and that this explains why they appear complementary at k=1 and yet compose badly. We test it by estimating, for every held-out task, the agent's per-instance solve probability from many independent rollouts under seven conditions: unconditioned, retrieved-experience memory, length-matched decoy memory, diversity-matched-by-temperature memory, GEPA-optimized instructions alone, GEPA instructions plus memory (the naive composition practitioners ship), and GEPA co-evolved with memory in the loop. From these pools we read off pass@k curves and their crossovers, a per-instance coverage decomposition into instances made newly solvable, made unsolvable, made more reliable, or made less reliable, and strategy-level solution diversity. Two controls decide the mechanism: raising temperature under memory until strategy diversity matches the unconditioned agent (if memory only sharpens, coverage returns; if it shifts the mode, it does not), and length-matched decoy memory (separating experience-specific narrowing from generic context load). The coupling test is the paper's centre: we ask whether the optimizer's gain carries the same coverage signature as memory's, whether the two concentrate onto the same or different strategy modes, and whether stacking them compounds coverage loss while sub-adding pass@1. Finally we test the fix the account implies and that the prompt-slot framing cannot express: a heterogeneous rollout portfolio that spends part of its budget unconditioned, part on memory, part on optimized instructions, constructed at zero extra compute by resampling the collected pools. All comparisons are instance-paired with unbiased pass@k estimators, two-level bootstrap intervals, null replicates, and matched-token as well as matched-k budgets.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED.** ReAct scaffold, tool stack, step limit, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from a training split with an ExpeL-style write path, then frozen for all test rollouts), prompt boilerplate, held-out split. Only the conditioning variant, decoding temperature (in one designated arm), and rollout-allocation policy vary.

**ENVIRONMENTS.** E1 (primary, carries every quantitative claim): tool-augmented multi-hop QA over HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue; the agent issues search calls, 4–8 model calls per episode. E2 (directional replication only): ALFWorld, step cap 20, where "strategy" is a concrete action sequence. **WebShop is cut** — it carried no claim the other two do not.

**MODELS.** Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (primary, full E1 grid), Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (secondary, decisive E1 arms). **Qwen3-32B is cut**; the claim is about conditioning, not scale, and two model families at two sizes is what the budget buys. A frontier API model performs offline bank distillation, GEPA reflection, and strategy annotation, identically across arms.

**PRECHECKS (gate the study, reported either way).** On a 150-instance dev split: (P-a) the memory bank must give a paired pass@1 gain ≥5 points over unconditioned at deployment temperature; (P-b) GEPA-optimized instructions must give a paired pass@1 gain ≥3 points. If a component does not help at k=1 there is no concentration to explain for that component; we enrich the bank / extend the GEPA budget until it passes, and report the precheck numbers rather than proceeding quietly.

**ARMS (E1, Llama-3.1-8B).**
- A0 Unconditioned.
- A1 Memory, top-7 retrieval (standard deployment).
- A3 Decoy memory: 7 items retrieved for a different query from a disjoint task family, token-matched to A1 within 5%. Adjudicates the generic-long-context account and the concurrent "any positive prior" account of 2605.28224.
- A4 Diversity-matched memory: A1 with temperature raised until mean distinct strategies per instance matches A0 within 5%, calibrated on dev only and frozen. **The decisive mechanism arm.**
- O1 GEPA-optimized instructions, no memory.
- O2 GEPA instructions (evolved memory-free) + memory at test — the naive composition.
- O3 GEPA co-evolved with memory in the loop + memory at test — the co-adaptation condition.

(The top-3 volume arm is **cut**: prior work already established injection volume as the pass@1 lever, and A3/A4 are what adjudicate mechanism.)

**ARMS (E2, 8B):** A0, A1, O1, O3.
**ARMS (E1, Qwen2.5-14B):** A0, A1, O1, O3.

**PORTFOLIO ARMS (zero additional rollouts, constructed by resampling collected pools).**
- P1 Heterogeneous portfolio: allocate k rollouts across {A0, A1, O1} on a simplex grid in steps of 0.25; report pass@k of the mixture. Endpoints reduce exactly to the homogeneous arms, so any interior peak cannot be a compute artifact.
- P2 Memory-as-reranker: k A0 rollouts, then one selection call in which retrieved memory items are shown alongside the k candidate trajectories. Costs one extra model call per draw (~5k calls total). Compared at matched total calls against A1 with self-consistency selection.

**CORE MEASUREMENT.** E1: 250 held-out instances × n=16 independent rollouts per arm at deployment temperature. E2: 100 instances × n=8. Unbiased combinatorial pass@k for k ∈ {1,2,4,8,16} (E1), {1,2,4,8} (E2).

**PRIMARY ENDPOINTS.**
1. **pass@k curves and crossovers** for each arm against A0, with bootstrap intervals on the crossover k*. Also reported on a matched-token axis, where shorter-prompt arms get proportionally more rollouts — the deployment-relevant comparison, since conditioning costs tokens on every rollout.
2. **Coverage decomposition.** Classify each instance by estimated solve probability under A0 versus the treatment arm: NEW (A0 never solves in n, treatment sometimes does), LOST (reverse), CONCENTRATED, DILUTED, NEITHER. Reported at the raw threshold, under a Jeffreys-prior posterior, and under two disjoint n=8 subsamples for split-half stability.
3. **Strategy diversity.** Each rollout reduced to a pre-registered canonical signature (E1: normalized sequence of search queries with entity/relation types; E2: sequence of primitive action types and target object classes), clustered per instance. Report distinct strategies per instance, first-tool-call entropy, and token-level self-BLEU on reasoning traces as a definition-free companion statistic. Signature extraction validated against 100 human-clustered instances (report adjusted Rand index).

**MECHANISM ANALYSES.**
(a) *Sharpening vs shifting.* Per instance, the fraction of A0's distinct strategies present in the treatment pool and vice versa. Pure sharpening predicts the treatment's strategies are a subset of A0's high-probability ones; shifting predicts strategies absent from A0's entire pool, plus elimination of strategies A0 used successfully. A4 is the causal version of the same test at the outcome level.
(b) *Mode identity across components — the coupling mechanism.* Jensen–Shannon divergence between per-instance strategy distributions of A1 and O1 (do memory and the optimizer concentrate onto the *same* mode?), and of O3 against A1 (does co-adaptation collapse the optimizer onto memory's mode?). This is the quantitative form of the track's "disjoint slices" observation.
(c) *LOST forensics.* On 60 LOST instances per component, annotate whether the conditioning recommended a strategy incompatible with the successful unconditioned strategy and whether the agent attempted it.
(d) *Bank-similarity moderator.* Per-instance max similarity to any bank item as a predictor of NEW vs LOST — if NEW concentrates on near-duplicates, memory's genuine coverage contribution is limited to task recurrence, which is the honest scope statement.

**RE-EXAMINATION TABLE.** For each component alone and for the naive composition, report the gain as it is normally reported (single sample, deployment temperature), then the same comparison at k=4 and at matched token budget. This is the direct statement of how much of a published-style memory / optimizer / memory+optimizer gain survives a sampling-aware protocol.

**RESOURCE ARITHMETIC.** E1-8B: 7 arms × 250 × 16 = 28,000 episodes, plus a 4,000-episode null replicate of A0 at a fresh seed set = 32,000. E1-14B: 4 × 250 × 16 = 16,000. E2-8B: 4 × 100 × 8 = 3,200. GEPA runs: 6 total (memory-free and memory-in-loop × {E1-8B, E1-14B, E2-8B}), each 40 candidates × 20 train instances × 2 rollouts = 1,600 episodes → 9,600. Total ≈ 61,000 episodes ≈ 352,000 model calls (E1 ~5 calls/episode, E2 ~20). At vLLM throughput on 4×A100 for 8B/14B this is ~3–4 days wall clock, within "days not weeks," and each configuration sits in the few-thousand-episode band the constraints assume. Portfolio arms add ~5k selection calls and no rollouts. API spend: GEPA reflection (~2M tokens), one-time bank distillation, and annotation/judging ≈ $180 total.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
(i) *A1 or O1 retaining its full advantage at k=8 and k=16* — the component adds genuine coverage, the concentration account is wrong for it, and we report that as vindication of the corresponding literature.
(ii) *A4 (diversity-matched memory)* — if decoding hotter under memory restores the unconditioned pass@k curve while keeping the pass@1 gain, memory is a pure sharpener, the fix is a hyperparameter, and the mode-shift claim dies while the measurement reframing survives. Single most important control.
(iii) *A3 (length-matched decoy)* — if irrelevant experience collapses coverage as much as A1, the phenomenon is generic context load, not experience. This also tests the concurrent 2605.28224 account, which predicts decoys (no positive priors about the query) should *not* collapse coverage.
(iv) *O1 as the missing baseline the reviewers named* — prompt-optimizer-only, run through the identical coverage pipeline. If O1 adds coverage while A1 destroys it, the "common currency" claim fails and the classical division-of-labour story stands.
(v) *O2/O3 beating both single components at k=8* — coupling works, our compounding prediction is wrong.
(vi) *Self-consistency over A1 rollouts at matched calls beating P1 and P2* — aggregation over memory-conditioned samples is already the best use of budget and the portfolio fix is unnecessary.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.** A4 discriminates sharpening from shifting at the outcome level; the strategy-overlap analysis does it at the trajectory level; the two must agree for the mechanism claim to stand. A3 removes content while holding tokens. O2 vs O3 isolates naive composition from co-adaptation (the drift question): O3 tells us whether letting the optimizer evolve *against* the memory absorbs the coverage loss or deepens it. P1's endpoints reduce exactly to A0/A1/O1, so the portfolio curve is an interpolation with all endpoints measured. A matched-token axis is reported for every arm so no conditioning is credited for spending more context. A shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check confirms retrieval functions.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Single-component (memory and optimizer alike):
1. On E1, each of A1 and O1 shows ≥5 points advantage over A0 at k=1 and ≤2 points by k=8, with crossover k* ≤ 8 for both models; on the matched-token axis, k* is smaller. (Stated as an equivalence claim at a 4-point margin at k=8; anything inside the band is reported inconclusive, not as support.)
2. Coverage: for each of A1 and O1, NEW instances are <4% of the test set and LOST/NEW ≥ 2 with exact binomial p<0.05 on discordant instances. Below that ratio we report the decomposition as inconclusive rather than as nesting.
3. Strategy diversity per instance falls ≥30% under A1 and ≥20% under O1 relative to A0, with matching drops in first-tool-call entropy.
4. **Mode shift, not sharpening:** under A4, with strategy diversity matched to A0, memory recovers less than half the pass@8 coverage gap, and ≥20% of A1's strategies are absent from A0's entire rollout pool.
5. A3 decoy memory reproduces less than half of A1's coverage loss.

Coupling (the track claim):
6. **Different modes:** per-instance strategy distributions of A1 and O1 are far apart (mean JSD ≥ 0.4, and ≥0.25 above the within-arm split-half JSD floor), while both are far from A0 — the quantitative form of "optimizer strong where memory weak."
7. **Stacking pays twice:** the naive composition O2 loses at least as much coverage at k=8 as the worse of A1 and O1 (LOST(O2) ≥ max(LOST(A1), LOST(O1)) within noise), while its pass@1 gain is strictly sub-additive: gain(O2) < gain(A1) + gain(O1) − 2 points.
8. **Co-adaptation is co-concentration:** O3 raises pass@1 over O2 by ≥2 points while its strategy distribution moves toward A1's (JSD(O3, A1) < JSD(O2, A1) by ≥0.1) and its pass@8 coverage is no better than O2's.
9. **The portfolio fix:** P1's optimum lies strictly in the interior of the simplex and beats the best homogeneous arm at matched k=8 by ≥3 points; equivalently, the union of solve sets from {A0, A1, O1} at k=4 each exceeds the best single arm at k=12 by ≥3 points.

**REFUTATION.** Advantages flat or growing in k, or NEW >8% with NEW exceeding LOST, kill the concentration claim for that component. If A4 restores the pass@8 gap to within 1 point, memory is a sharpener and the mode-shift claim is dead. If A3 reproduces A1's loss in full, the paper is about injected context volume, not experience, and we reframe explicitly. If O1 shows no coverage loss, the common-currency claim fails and we report that memory and prompt optimization are genuinely different animals — a clean negative for our central thesis. If P1's optimum is at a vertex, the constructive corollary is empty.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Many rollouts per instance are collected by construction, so estimates and their uncertainty come from the same data.
(a) **pass@k estimation:** standard unbiased combinatorial estimator per instance from n rollouts, averaged over instances; intervals from a two-level bootstrap resampling instances (10k resamples) and, within instance, rollouts, so instance heterogeneity and finite-rollout noise both propagate. All arms share instances, so every comparison is instance-paired.
(b) **Primary tests:** exact McNemar on paired fix/break counts at k=1 with the full decomposition always shown; paired bootstrap on per-instance pass@k differences for k>1; Holm correction across the arm family within each endpoint. Crossover k* reported with a bootstrap interval, never as a point.
(c) **Null replicates:** A0 is re-run on E1 with a disjoint seed set (4,000 episodes); the distribution of apparent pass@k deltas between the two identical arms defines the noise floor at every k, and no effect is claimed unless it exceeds that distribution's 95th percentile. Load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.
(d) **Coverage-decomposition noise:** NEW/LOST are thresholds on noisy rates, so they are reported at n=16, on two disjoint n=8 subsamples (split-half stability), and under a Jeffreys posterior giving the probability an instance is truly zero-rate. No NEW-vs-LOST difference smaller than the split-half instability is interpreted; the pre-registered claim threshold is LOST/NEW ≥ 2 with exact binomial p<0.05.
(e) **Minimum detectable effect:** with 250 paired E1 instances at n=16, the two-level bootstrap gives SE ≈ 1.7 points on a paired pass@k difference for k ≤ 8, so the design detects ~4.5 points at 80% power. Every quantitative prediction above is stated at or beyond that threshold, and the k=8 equivalence claim uses a 4-point margin. E2 at 100 instances × n=8 has roughly double the SE and is explicitly directional replication, not evidence for a numeric threshold.
(f) **Frozen calibration:** the A4 temperature and all GEPA optimization use dev/train splits only and are frozen before test rollouts. GEPA candidate selection uses its own validation split, never the test instances.
(g) **Portfolio estimator validity:** rollouts are independent given (instance, arm), so mixture pass@k estimated by resampling across arm pools is unbiased for a deployed heterogeneous portfolio; intervals come from the same two-level bootstrap.
Preprint Collision Check:
The search returned one genuine collision and several near misses; I treat the collision as prior work rather than arguing it away.

**COLLIDES, PARTIALLY: "When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?" (arXiv 2605.28224).** This paper already places retrieved fact/experience memory inside multi-trajectory tool-use inference and argues for a diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff that no retrieval policy escapes, with the mechanism "any positive prior facts in the prompt bias the model toward consistency." That is the same causal story as our memory-side hypothesis in the same experimental regime. I therefore drop any claim to having discovered that memory reduces trajectory diversity, and cite it as concurrent prior work. What survives, and what this proposal is now organized around: (i) it does not measure whether the *solve set* shrinks — diversity loss with intact coverage is a different and benign outcome, and our NEW/LOST decomposition is the test that separates them; (ii) it has no diversity-matched-temperature control, so it cannot distinguish sharpening from mode shift, which is the difference between "raise the temperature" and "restructure the deployment"; (iii) its "any positive prior" account makes a prediction our length-matched decoy arm can falsify; (iv) it contains no prompt optimizer, so it says nothing about whether instruction search carries the same signature, whether the two components concentrate onto the same mode, or what happens when they are stacked or co-adapted — which is the assigned coupling question and now the centre of this proposal.

**"How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (arXiv 2505.16067, ACL 2026)** — experience-following: high input-memory similarity produces highly similar outputs, causing error propagation. Mechanistic support for our account, framed as long-horizon degradation; no pass@k, no coverage, no optimizer. Does not collide; strengthens our bank-similarity moderator analysis, which we now frame as a direct test of experience-following at the coverage level.

**Training-time diversity collapse: 2509.06941, 2509.04784, R-Diverse (2602.13103), DyJR (2603.16157), Exploratory Memory-Augmented LLM Agent (2602.23008).** All are weight-space or RL-loop interventions; 2602.23008 asserts static memory limits diversity but proposes a joint-RL fix rather than measuring the trade. None collides; together they establish the phenomenon for gradients, which is precisely why the training-free analogue and the optimizer-side extension are worth nailing down.

**Retrieval × aggregation: 2412.10684** (single-turn RAG, retrieval interacting with self-consistency, passage-permutation fix) and **2511.00751** (capability, not context, explains diminishing sampling returns — a competing explanation we control for by measuring A0's own curve). **2404.16807** measures lexical, not strategy-level, diversity. **"Leveraging LLM Inconsistency to Boost Pass@k" (2505.12938)** runs the opposite direction and is a useful counterpoint for the portfolio arm.

**HONEST CAVEATS.** The search budget was exhausted before I could characterize three borderline titles (MemCollab, ParamMem, Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory) or sweep 2026 OpenReview submissions. Given 2605.28224 exists, I now assume a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure exists somewhere in the 2026 memory literature; the proposal is written so that its contribution does not depend on that figure being absent. What no retrieved work does is measure solve-set coverage loss, adjudicate sharpening versus mode shift, or ask whether prompt optimization is the same kind of device as memory.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Concurrent-work risk is real, not hypothetical.** 2605.28224 already owns "memory costs diversity in multi-trajectory tool-use inference." If a follow-up adds coverage curves before we publish, our remaining contribution is the optimizer-coupling half (common currency, mode divergence, compounding under stacking, portfolio fix). We have deliberately made that half the paper's spine rather than an appendix, so the contribution degrades gracefully.
2. **pass@k saturation** could compress the crossover into an uninterpretable region; mitigated by selecting instance pools with unconditioned pass@1 in the 30–60% band on dev and reporting full curves.
3. **NEW/LOST is a threshold on noisy rates.** n=16 cannot certify an instance is truly unsolvable without conditioning; the nesting claim is stated as "nested at n=16" with split-half stability and a pre-registered LOST/NEW ≥ 2 evidentiary bar, not as a claim about policy support.
4. **Strategy signatures are a design surface** that could manufacture the diversity result; the definition is fixed in advance, published verbatim, validated against human clustering (ARI reported), and accompanied by definition-free self-BLEU.
5. **A4 may not be achievable** — temperature might not reach A0's diversity without destroying coherence. We then report the achieved diversity level and treat A4 as partial rather than clean, and lean on the trajectory-level overlap analysis for the sharpening/shifting call.
6. **GEPA may not clear its precheck** on a 8B agent for these tasks. If P-b fails after an extended search budget, we report that and reinterpret O1 as "best hand-plus-search instruction found," which weakens the optimizer-specific claim to a claim about optimized instructions generally; we say so rather than quietly relabeling.
7. **Single bank, single optimizer.** Results may depend on bank composition (general heuristics may narrow more than episodic near-duplicates) and on GEPA's particular reflective operator; the bank-similarity moderator is our only within-study handle, and MIPRO is not run — a scope limit we state rather than paper over.
8. **Compute forced real cuts:** WebShop, the 32B model, and the injection-volume arm are gone; long-horizon evidence is E2-only and directional, at roughly double the E1 standard error.
9. **The portfolio payload presupposes k>1 deployments.** For strictly single-sample deployments the paper's message is a measurement warning and a caution about stacking conditioners, not a method.
10. **A refusal, stated plainly:** reviewers asked for a smaller, safer design. We cut breadth (environments, models, arms) but did not soften the claim into "we measure the interaction." The prediction that coupling *compounds coverage loss while sub-adding pass@1* is the risky part, and it is preserved with numeric thresholds and explicit refutation conditions.
